mechanism_summary: Namespace yard-ops carries the label pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted while its warn and audit labels and its approved-level annotation say baseline, so the Pod Security admission plugin rejects every new gate-checkin pod as 'violates PodSecurity "restricted:latest"' (allowPrivilegeEscalation, capabilities, runAsNonRoot, seccompProfile) and the release ReplicaSet cannot create a single pod while the two old pods of the same template keep serving.
decisive_evidence: ReplicaSet FailedCreate events in namespace yard-ops with message 'Error creating: pods "gate-checkin-<hash>-<id>" is forbidden: violates PodSecurity "restricted:latest": allowPrivilegeEscalation != false (container "kiosk" must set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation=false), unrestricted capabilities (container "kiosk" must set securityContext.capabilities.drop=["ALL"]), runAsNonRoot != true (pod or container "kiosk" must set securityContext.runAsNonRoot=true), seccompProfile (pod or container "kiosk" must set securityContext.seccompProfile.type to "RuntimeDefault" or "Localhost")' (also carried on the Deployment's ReplicaFailure condition); namespace yard-ops labels pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted, warn=baseline, audit=baseline and annotation security.northbound.example/approved-level=baseline; deployment yard-ops/gate-checkin at 2/3 ready, 0 updated, Progressing=False ProgressDeadlineExceeded, with the old ReplicaSet's pods of the identical template Running and Ready.
remediation_summary: Set the namespace's enforce level back to the approved one - kubectl label namespace yard-ops pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline --overwrite - after which the new ReplicaSet creates its pods and the release completes to 3 of 3 updated with no change to deployment yard-ops/gate-checkin; removing the enforce label entirely is the interim mitigation if the platform team wants to re-run its rollout.
